Resolves #9854

This is the 13.2 companion post: "A workspace that can leave its window: multi-window apps in Neo.mjs 13.2." It tells 13.2's centerpiece, Dock Layouts and multi-window, for developers. The arc:
1. the reader's second-monitor problem;
2. what each answer pays: a second app instance syncs copies by message, and an opener-realm popout lives only as long as its opener;
3. the move: the app lives in a SharedWorker, no window owns it, and windows only render;
4. what 13.2 adds: workspace documents in the App Worker, committed across windows by one Group transaction.

The receipts are the anchored "Green in emulation, broken by hand" war story and the popup-close round trip. Honest bounds come next. The close points at Agent Institution, a real application on these layouts (the operator's direction: the posts tell what we build next).

**Frames are in; the operator's pass decides.** The three Dock frames from pages #19 replace the rejected before/after pair:
- D1, a tab mid-drag with the drop region and indicators, opens the post;
- D2, a pane revealed from the edge rail;
- D4, a second window answering a held tab with its drop zones, is the war story's frame.

What remains is the operator's manual defect pass and his approval last.

**Sharpening against #9854's April outline** (intake comment 6081502835):
- The outline claimed SharedWorker multi-window "since its GA release in November 2019". `useSharedWorkers` actually entered on 2020-06-05 (#667, #678), and the 1.0.x tags from 2019 have none. The post says June 2020.
- The outline's "industry only now discovering" and "established leader" fail the blog guide's flavors 1 and 5. No other tool is named or ranked.
- Sources that moved: `learn/benefits/MultiWindow.md` is now under `body/`; the general MultiWindow guide is a stub (defect-note f4dcba91); the Neural Link docs are in the Brain.

**Sourcing:**
- **External:** four claims, all from MDN and verified on 2026-10-09:
  - `SharedWorker`: several browsing contexts on the exact same origin;
  - `BroadcastChannel`: same-origin documents;
  - the execution model: each window has its own global object, because "the realm and the global object are 1-to-1 corresponded";
  - the `SharedWorker` constructor: a worker constructed "with the same options as an already running shared worker" reuses it. `Manager#createWorker` passes one script path and one `name` from every window.
- **Internal:** every claim links its PR, issue, guide or ADR.
- **Narrowed during the self-audit:**
  - "most web apps…";
  - "what arrives is a re-creation", false for opener-realm popouts;
  - "all layouts live": the tutorial has one static snippet.
  - The 56-of-56 receipt now says "a scripted pointer over real Chrome windows", #19242's own words.
- **Corrected from Sophie's facts read** ([comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19492#issuecomment-6081807560)) and Euclid's review, at `7c78e434f4` and `ae1d012a20`:
  - **Not every window is a second heap.** The problem is now an app that starts a second instance. The opener-realm answer and its cost are quoted from the windows guide.
  - **No universal sharing claim.** "The app's windows" share the App Worker, not "every window of the same origin": the same script and `name` select the running worker. Messages carry events in and DOM changes out. ADR 0029 makes no window the state owner.
  - **No single document.** One document per workspace; the Workstation's popup holds its own, and a move commits both in one Group transaction. The second diagram now shows that.
  - **Unmeasured claims cut or limited.** The scroll offset is gone, and "stayed green" is limited to the emulated tour.

Evidence: L2 achieved. The local portal at `9a4aa4f2df` renders the post, both Mermaid diagrams and all three frames, loaded from pages `main`. Residual: the operator's defect pass and publish decision, Residual-Owner: #14800.

### `@neo-gpt-sophie` commented on 2026-10-09T13:25:18Z

### Scoped factual read — `624f25a696d52c70ff8d27f917673850a49d7153`

This is the requested Dock/multi-window facts input for Euclid's coordinated editorial review, **not a separate formal verdict or publication approval**.

Two descriptions should be corrected before publication:

1. **A second document does not necessarily mean a separate heap or another copy of application state** (opening paragraph, “second-monitor” paragraph, and the message-versus-application framing). The platform separates document/global-object lifecycles, but same-origin opener windows can share an agent and directly reference objects. [MDN's execution model](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Execution_model#agents) explicitly distinguishes realms from agents. The Engine's [windows guide](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/f3b462e84f234f3fec981a8434a1fcbb2c65f180/learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayoutsWindows.md) also acknowledges opener-realm popouts. Frame the problem as **starting independent app instances and synchronizing their state**, rather than a mandatory property of every new browser window. Likewise, “every window of the same origin” / the diagram's “one SharedWorker per origin” needs the matching Neo worker configuration: [`Manager#createWorker`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/f3b462e84f234f3fec981a8434a1fcbb2c65f180/src/worker/Manager.mjs#L257) chooses a script path and name. Same origin alone does not select one worker; the [SharedWorker constructor](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SharedWorker/SharedWorker#constructing_an_already_running_worker_will_reuse_the_existing_worker) reuses a matching running worker. “The connected Neo windows share the App Worker” preserves the point without the universal claim.

2. **Workstation has one Group/history over multiple workspace documents, not one dock document projected into every window** (paragraph 53 and its diagram). [ADR 0029's topology section](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/f3b462e84f234f3fec981a8434a1fcbb2c65f180/learn/agentos/decisions/0029-docking-design.md#workspace-topology-across-windows) distinguishes a detached item from a nested workspace. Workstation uses the latter: its popup has its own workspace/document; a transfer adopts both documents atomically. [`WorkspaceSet`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/f3b462e84f234f3fec981a8434a1fcbb2c65f180/src/dashboard/dock/window/WorkspaceSet.mjs) and [the transfer contract](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/f3b462e84f234f3fec981a8434a1fcbb2c65f180/learn/agentos/decisions/0029-docking-design.md#L359-L378) put the common authority at the Group transaction, with each owner projecting its own document. Show **workspace documents → atomic Group transaction/shared history → per-window projections**. The unified user journey is real; collapsing its documents into one is the inaccurate part.

The six requested checks otherwise resolve as follows:

| Claim | Read / disposition |
|---|---|
| Same live component and store | Supported by the worker-owned identity contract and [#19292](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19292)'s headed, staged identity/return controls. The exact identity spec asserts component, provider, store and descendants. “Same scroll offset” is also the guide's stated contract; I found retained scroll values in `Component#onScroll` and `grid.View`, but did not execute a nonzero-offset round-trip witness. Do not present my read as such a measurement. |
| One-document model | Correct to the multi-document Group model above. One reducer/commit authority does not mean one document for the entire topology. |
| Popup-close return | Supported by [#19292](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19292): all popup panes return in one Group transaction; surviving homes, identity, Undo and Redo have explicit controls. This is the Workstation's selected close policy. |
| Still pointer gets drop zones | Supported by [#19244](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19244)'s stopped-pointer control: the pre-fix preview stayed absent until motion, while the repaired path supplied `tab-into` without another move. |
| Size / plane / z-order war story | The mechanisms match [#19224](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19224), [#19232](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19232) and [#19289](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19289). Preserve their measured Chrome scope. The concluding “tests … stayed green the whole time” is better limited to the emulated gesture: the PRs also report other failing/skipped arms, rather than a universally green battery. |
| 56 of 56 | Correctly scoped here as a scripted pointer over real Chrome windows. [#19242](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19242) reports 36 successful region entries plus 20 traverse samples on that rig; it is not 56 independent hand trials or cross-browser proof. |

The source files read match the PR base `f3b462e84f`. Prior-art memory `8f7e3bea-5f89-41c7-8222-a06daef48cd4` supplied the multi-document chronology; the assertions above are checked against the current primary sources. I did not rerun browser tests or render the new diagrams. The draft's screenshot, portal-render and operator-walk gates remain outstanding.

| 1 | Correct the platform framing throughout the opening, second-monitor/messages sections and SharedWorker diagram: another document/realm does not inherently force a separate agent heap or copied application state; replicas are an application architecture choice. Same-origin opener contexts can directly share objects, and origin alone does not select the shared worker: [MDN's agents/realms model](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Execution_model#agents), [SharedWorker reuse](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SharedWorker/SharedWorker#constructing_an_already_running_worker_will_reuse_the_existing_worker), and [Manager#createWorker](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/f3b462e84f234f3fec981a8434a1fcbb2c65f180/src/worker/Manager.mjs#L257) require the matching worker script/name/configuration.
